adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: An older adult with progressive magnetic gait, urinary dysfunction, frontal-executive slowing, and ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal enlargement has idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus. Parkinson disease and Alzheimer disease do not explain the clinicoradiologic combination.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Parkinson disease can cause gait freezing and urinary symptoms in advanced disease, but the disproportionate ventriculomegaly plus early magnetic gait, bladder dysfunction, and frontal-subcortical slowing makes NPH uniquely best. Alzheimer disease lacks the classic gait-first CSF-dynamics phenotype.
